title: Circuit-aware regional handoff with load-shedding thresholds and model-variant degradation mapping
creator: Ethan Cole
description:
Objective: Implement an orchestrator component and a set of deterministic readiness checks that perform circuit-aware regional handoffs. The goal is to reduce failover blast radius and avoid cold-start regression by combining capacity-aware thresholds, load-shedding policies, and an explicit model-variant degradation map that informs automatic fallback behavior.

Background: We’ve observed two recurring failure modes during cross-region cutovers: (1) large latency spikes caused by cold KV/cache misses and model weight page-ins, and (2) incorrect fallback decisions that route traffic to a variant whose tokenizer/sequence-length profile increases cost or error rates. This ticket introduces a scoring-based gate and a staged activation protocol that verifies a region’s operational posture before accepting steady-state traffic.

Scope: Implement the orchestrator logic in the routing plane, add probe implementations for the runtime agents (cache-sampled probe, tokenized-sample-run, memory-occupancy probe), instrument telemetry into Console dashboards, and provide automated rollback AND partial-traffic fallback to model-variants with explicit degradation profiles. This work must be compatible with Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments.

Non-goals: Model retraining, large-scale data migrations, or changing customer routing policies outside the orchestrator surface. We do not change quota semantics in this ticket.

Design summary:
- Scoring model: compose three normalized scores into a readiness_score -> capacity_score (0-100), cache_warmth_score (0-100), model_compat_score (0-100). readiness_score = weighted(sum). Default weights: capacity 0.5, cache 0.3, compat 0.2. Gate opens when readiness_score >= 80 and no single score < 50.
- Circuit-awareness: use per-region circuit state (open/half-open/closed) tracked in the control plane. If a circuit is half-open we permit only canary flows (1-5% routing) with progressive ramp and strict latency/err-rate SLOs.
- Load-shedding: when capacity_score < threshold (default 60), shed non-critical routes (batch/long-running reranks) before shedding chat/generation. Configurable policy table per customer tier.
- Model-variant map: maintain an ordered fallback list per model family where each variant has an associated degradation_profile string (e.g., "latency+5%, quality-2pts, cost-0.6x"). The orchestrator uses the map to pick the least-harmful fallback when the primary variant is unavailable or the region cannot meet latency SLOs.
- Probes implemented: kernel-resident-check (are key modules loaded into GPU/CPU memory), kv-sample-probe (run cached prefixes to measure hit rate & latency), tokenized-sample-run (run canonical prompt set at production sequence lengths), dependency-health (KMS/metrics/agent heartbeats).
- Telemetry: emit readiness_score breakdown, probe timestamps, probe traces, and reason-code when gate fails. Expose in Console as a per-region readiness timeline and per-activation trace linking to PRs and audits.

Compatibility considerations: For Private deployments we read the same readiness config but allow operator overrides. For Dedicated pools the capacity_score uses pool reservation info rather than global autoscaler state.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator computes readiness_score and prevents routing when readiness_score < 80
Canary flow supports staged ramp 0->1%->5%->20%->100% with automated rollback on violations
KV-sample-probe reports cache_warmth_score and matches offline simulation within +/-10% for hit-rate
Model-variant fallback chooses the declared variant with the minimal predicted quality loss per degradation_profile
Console shows per-region readiness timeline, probe-level reasons for gate failures, and a single-click rollback
Integration tests simulate a regional failure and verify traffic ramps to fallback region with load-shedding applied to non-critical routes
Private and Dedicated deploys accept operator overrides but log the override reason and require an audit tag
tasks: Define readiness scoring proto and default weights
Implement probes in runtime-agent (kv-sample, tokenized-run, kernel-resident)
Implement orchestrator state machine and circuit model in routing-control-plane
Add model-variant degradation metadata to model registry and expose via API
Console dashboard: readiness timeline + probe trace links
Automated integration tests (chaos-simulated region failover + canary verification)
Create runbook and emergency rollback playbook
Documentation: README, operator-overrides guide, and changelog entry
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature-flagged deployment to staging cluster and a single non-critical region. Run integration tests and synthetic traffic for 72h. Phase 2: Enable canary traffic (1%) to two regions, monitor for 48h. Phase 3: Increase to 5% and verify SLOs for 24h. Phase 4: Enable 20% then 100% after 72h of stable metrics. If canary_error_rate > 0.5% or probe_latency_ms p95 exceeds baseline+150ms during ramp, automatically rollback to previous routing policy.
